page: Microsoft Azure M32ts is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 38 MB L3. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1049 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a significant performance divergence between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is consistently low, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks (gzip and bzip3) all scoring in the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression placing in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average performance, yielding 1220.51 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 106.41 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Database operations, static web serving throughput, and Redis SET operations at 20.68 million operations per second all perform within the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the M32ts instance is its weak single-threaded processing capability, which limits its suitability for serialized tasks. However, its dedicated 32 vCPUs and 192.0 GB memory profile offer a balanced resource density for multi-threaded workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a substantial memory allocation and local storage capacity without the premium cost of GPU hardware. It is suited for workloads such as multi-threaded database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate-scale LLM inference, where multi-core execution can offset the lower single-core clock efficiency.

It features 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores), 192.0 GB of RAM, and 1049 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. Benchmark results indicate a clear performance tradeoff: single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks fall into the bottom 10% tier, whereas multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations consistently achieve average (middle 50%) ratings.
